answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to complete a sequential, identity-bound delay before it can earn: a falcon cannot fly two routes at once, and a verifiable delay function works the same way, step after step, with each step depending on the last. The work is tied to one public key, so it cannot be whispered to another identity or reused, and buying more machines does not shorten one chain. Growing a garden of fake identities then costs calendar time per fake, not just money, because every extra identity must wait out its own full delay.
